---
title: "Classifying Instruction Condition from Eye-Movement Transitions"
author: "John Zbaracki"
output: github_document
---

## Overview

Children received speech-only or speech-and-gesture instruction on mathematical equivalence problems, and their eye movements were recorded while they solved posttest problems. Children's eye-movements were recorded during pretest, training, and posttest, but only posttest is analyzed here. 


Question: Do children's eye-movement patterns differ depending on how they were taught, and can a classifier recover the instruction condition from those patterns alone?

Data: Each row is one posttest problem for one participant. Gaze was coded into areas of interest (AOIs). Each number in the problem as well as the blank were considered an AOI. AOIs were coded left to right e.g. 1 + 2 + 3 = _ + 3 would be AOI A AOI B AOI C AOI D AOI E. Likewise, 4 + 5 + 6 = 4 + _ would be coded the same with AOI A AOI B AOI C AOI D AOI E. Note AOIs are coded by location and not element - so therefore the blank can be AOI 4 or 5. Predictors are counts of transitions between AOIs (e.g., `AB` = a look from A directly to B).

Approach: Radial-kernel support vector machines (`caret`), trained on balanced groups and repeated over 64 random seeds. Models predicting a random A/B split of participants serve as a null baseline.

Results: Condition models reached 62% accuracy versus a baseline of 50 while our randomized control test showed only near 55% accuracy. 

Data availability: Participant data are not included in this repository.

## Blank-relative transition coding

Transitions are recoded relative to the blank's position, so the same columns mean the same thing whether the blank is on the left (`LB`) or right (`RB`): `Blank` is the blank's AOI and `RA` is the other right-side AOI.


```{r blank-coding}
FinalData.Outcome.Blank = FinalData.Outcome %>%
  mutate('ABlank' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ AD,
                              BlankLocation == "RB" ~ AE)) %>%
  mutate('BBlank' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ BD,
                              BlankLocation == "RB" ~ BE)) %>%
  mutate('CBlank' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ CD,
                              BlankLocation == "RB" ~ CE)) %>%
  mutate('BlankBlank' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ DD,
                              BlankLocation == "RB" ~ EE)) %>%
  mutate('RABlank' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ ED,
                              BlankLocation == "RB" ~ DE)) %>%
  mutate('BlankA' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ DA,
                              BlankLocation == "RB" ~ EA)) %>%
  mutate('BlankB' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ DB,
                              BlankLocation == "RB" ~ EB)) %>%
  mutate('BlankC' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ DC,
                              BlankLocation == "RB" ~ EC)) %>%
  mutate('BlankRA' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ DE,
                              BlankLocation == "RB" ~ ED)) %>%
  mutate('ARA' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ AE,
                           BlankLocation == "RB" ~ AD)) %>%
  mutate('BRA' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ BE,
                           BlankLocation == "RB" ~ BD)) %>%
  mutate('CRA' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ CE,
                           BlankLocation == "RB" ~ CD)) %>%
  mutate('RARA' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ EE,
                           BlankLocation == "RB" ~ DD)) %>%
  mutate('RAA' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ EA,
                           BlankLocation == "RB" ~ DA)) %>%
  mutate('RAB' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ EB,
                           BlankLocation == "RB" ~ DB)) %>%
  mutate('RAC' = case_when(BlankLocation == "LB" ~ EC,
                           BlankLocation == "RB" ~ DC)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(AD, AE, BD, BE, CD, CE, DD, DE, EE, ED, DA, DB, DC, EA, EB, EC))

```




## Helper functions

### Random A/B participant assignment (null baseline)

Randomly splits participants into two groups (A/B), with half of each instruction condition in each group. Because these labels are random, a model predicting A/B should perform at chance (50%), which gives a baseline for interpreting the condition models.


```{r fn-ab-assignment}
ABFunct = function(FuncInputData) {
  
  Participants = unique(FuncInputData$ParticipantID)
  Participants.GE = FuncInputData %>%
    filter(Condition == "Speech and Gesture") %>%
    group_by(ParticipantID) %>%
    summarize()

  Participants.NG = FuncInputData %>%
    filter(Condition == "Speech Only") %>%
    group_by(ParticipantID) %>%
    summarize()
    
  randomSample.GE = sort(sample(1:length(Participants.GE$ParticipantID), round(length(Participants.GE$ParticipantID)/2, digits = 0), replace=FALSE))
  randomSample.NG = sort(sample(1:length(Participants.NG$ParticipantID), round(length(Participants.NG$ParticipantID)/2, digits = 0), replace=FALSE))

  GEPart = Participants.GE$ParticipantID[c(randomSample.GE)]
  NGPart = Participants.NG$ParticipantID[c(randomSample.NG)]

  PartTrainList = append(NGPart, GEPart)

  FinalData.AB = FuncInputData %>%
    mutate(AORB = case_when(ParticipantID %in% PartTrainList == TRUE ~ "A",
                            ParticipantID %in% PartTrainList != TRUE ~ "B"
  ))
  return(FinalData.AB)
}
```


### Balance groups: A/B

The balancing functions downsample each group to the size of the smallest group, so a classifier can't reach high accuracy just by predicting the majority class.

```{r fn-balance-ab}
EqGroupsFunct.AORB = function(TrainTestData){
  
  Total = TrainTestData %>%
  group_by(AORB)%>%
  summarize(total = n()) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  ungroup()
  

  AGroup = TrainTestData %>% filter(AORB == "A") %>%
   .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]


  BGroup = TrainTestData %>%
  filter(AORB == "B") %>%
  .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]

  ABData.Eq = rbind(AGroup, BGroup)
  
  return(ABData.Eq)
}

```

### Balance groups: instruction condition

```{r fn-balance-condition}
EqGroupsFunct = function(TrainTestData){
  
  Total = TrainTestData %>%
  group_by(Condition)%>%
  summarize(total = n()) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  ungroup()
  
  SO = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(Condition == 'Speech Only') %>%
   .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]

  GE = TrainTestData %>%
  filter(Condition == 'Speech and Gesture') %>%
  .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]

  ABData.Eq = rbind(GE, SO)
  
  return(ABData.Eq)
}

```


### Balance groups: condition × problem matching

```{r fn-balance-condition-matching}
EqGroupsFunct.ProbFeatures = function(TrainTestData){
  
  Total = TrainTestData %>%
  group_by(Condition, Matching)%>%
  summarize(total = n()) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  ungroup()
  
  SO.MA = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(Condition == 'Speech Only' & Matching == "Matching") %>%
   .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]

  GE.MA = TrainTestData %>%
  filter(Condition == 'Speech and Gesture' & Matching == "Matching") %>%
  .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]

  SO.NMA = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(Condition == 'Speech Only' & Matching != "Matching") %>%
   .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]

  GE.NMA = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(Condition == 'Speech and Gesture' & Matching != "Matching") %>%
  .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]
  
  ABData.Eq = rbind(SO.MA, GE.MA)
  ABData.Eq = rbind(ABData.Eq, SO.NMA)
  ABData.Eq = rbind(ABData.Eq, GE.NMA)

  return(ABData.Eq)
}

```


### Balance groups: A/B × problem matching

```{r fn-balance-ab-matching}
EqGroupsFunct.ProbFeatures.AORB = function(TrainTestData){
  
  Total = TrainTestData %>%
  group_by(AORB, Matching)%>%
  summarize(total = n()) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  ungroup()
  
  A.MA = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(AORB == 'A' & Matching == "Matching") %>%
   .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]

  B.MA = TrainTestData %>%
  filter(AORB == 'B' & Matching == "Matching") %>%
  .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]

  A.NMA = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(AORB == 'A' & Matching != "Matching") %>%
   .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]

  B.NMA = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(AORB == 'B' & Matching != "Matching") %>%
  .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total$total), replace = FALSE),]
  
  ABData.Eq = rbind(A.MA, B.MA)
  ABData.Eq = rbind(ABData.Eq, A.NMA)
  ABData.Eq = rbind(ABData.Eq, B.NMA)

  return(ABData.Eq)
}

```

### Balance groups: condition × correctness (equal cells)

```{r fn-balance-condition-correctness}
EqGroupsFunct.Correctness.GE = function(TrainTestData){
  
#We have to take the smallest available data set or it will guess correct every single time - insturction must be equalized AND correctness must be equalized.

  Total.Incorr = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(ProbCorrAdj == 0) %>%
    group_by(Condition, ProbCorrAdj)%>%
    summarize(total = n()) %>%
    na.omit() %>%
    ungroup()
  
  SO.Corr = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(Condition == 'Speech Only' & ProbCorrAdj == 1) %>%
   .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total.Incorr$total), replace = FALSE),]

  GE.Corr = TrainTestData %>%
  filter(Condition == 'Speech and Gesture' & ProbCorrAdj == 1) %>%
  .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total.Incorr$total), replace = FALSE),]

  SO.Incorr = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(Condition == 'Speech Only' & ProbCorrAdj == 0) %>%
   .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total.Incorr$total), replace = FALSE),]

  GE.Incorr = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(Condition == 'Speech and Gesture' & ProbCorrAdj == 0) %>%
  .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total.Incorr$total), replace = FALSE),]
  
  ABData.Eq = rbind(SO.Corr, GE.Corr)
  ABData.Eq = rbind(ABData.Eq, SO.Incorr)
  ABData.Eq = rbind(ABData.Eq, GE.Incorr)

  return(ABData.Eq)
}

```

### Balance groups: correctness only

```{r fn-balance-correctness}
EqGroupsFunct.Correctness = function(TrainTestData){
  
  Total.Corr = TrainTestData %>%
    group_by(ProbCorrAdj)%>%
    summarize(total = n()) %>%
    na.omit() %>%
    ungroup()

  Corr = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(ProbCorrAdj == 1) %>%
   .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total.Corr$total), replace = FALSE),]

  Incorr = TrainTestData %>%
    filter(ProbCorrAdj == 0) %>%
   .[sample(nrow(.), size = min(Total.Corr$total), replace = FALSE),]

  ABData.Eq = rbind(Corr, Incorr)

  return(ABData.Eq)
}

```


*All chunks above must be run before any of the models below.*

## Models: predicting instruction condition

Each model is fit 64 times with different random seeds. Each repetition balances the groups, makes an 80/20 train/test split, tunes a radial-kernel SVM with leave-one-out cross-validation, and records the cross-validated accuracy and the held-out test accuracy.


### Condition ~ transitions

```{r con-transitions}

seeds = c(42,102,42341,52,3948, 3723, 3153, 2666, 296, 489, 871, 4825, 2570, 103, 513, 1118, 296, 3043, 2028, 4091, 99, 3357, 2637, 4696, 2320, 3705, 2546, 170, 63, 50, 4830, 18, 727, 438, 182, 6583, 4982, 492, 6784, 59201, 5893, 2069, 3903, 6943, 4032, 201, 56965, 4923, 102134, 2403, 2983, 5943, 2043, 6938, 59, 1111, 32212, 3912, 69043, 2934, 103, 192, 104586, 98453)

AccuracyValList = matrix(0,64,1)

AccuracyValList = as.data.frame(AccuracyValList)
colnames(AccuracyValList) = c("AccuracyValue")

ConMLTestData_64.ConOnly = matrix(0,0,0)


j = 1 
for(j in 1:64){
  set.seed(seeds[j])
  
  ConTraining = EqGroupsFunct(FinalData.Outcome)

  intrain <- createDataPartition(y = ConTraining$Condition, p= 0.8, list = FALSE)
  training <- ConTraining[intrain,]
  testing <- ConTraining[-intrain,]
  testingSave = testing
  
  training = training %>% 
  select(-c(ParticipantID, TestTime, ProblemTime, BlankLocation, Matching, ProblemNumber, ProbDuration, SubjectGender, Outcome, ProbCorrAdj)) %>%
  mutate(Condition = factor(.$Condition))
  
  testing = testing %>% 
  select(-c(ParticipantID, TestTime, ProblemTime, BlankLocation, Matching, ProblemNumber, ProbDuration, SubjectGender, Outcome, ProbCorrAdj)) %>%
  mutate(Condition = factor(.$Condition)) 
  
  trctrl <- trainControl(method = "LOOCV")#, number = 10, repeats = 10)
  svmRadial.Con <- train(Condition~., data = training, method = "svmRadial",
                 trControl=trctrl,
                 preProcess = c("center", "scale"),
                 tuneLength = 15)
  AccuracyValList$AccuracyValue[j] = max(svmRadial.Con$results$Accuracy)
  test_pred <- predict(svmRadial.Con, newdata = testing)
  TestData = cbind(testingSave, test_pred)
  TestData.Pred = TestData %>% 
    mutate(PredCorr = case_when(test_pred == Condition ~ 1,
                              test_pred != Condition ~ 0))
  testPredData = confusionMatrix(test_pred, testing$Condition)
  AccuracyValList$TestAccuracy[j] = testPredData$overall[1]
  AccuracyValList$Model[[j]] = svmRadial.Con
  TestData.Pred$MLSet = j

  ConMLTestData_64.ConOnly = rbind(ConMLTestData_64.ConOnly,TestData.Pred)
  print(j)
  print(Sys.time())
}

```

  trctrl <- trainControl(method = "LOOCV")

                 tuneLength = 15)

  ConTraining = EqGroupsFunct.Correctness(FinalData.Outcome)

  intrain <- createDataPartition(y = ConTraining$ProbCorrAdj, p= 0.8, list = FALSE)
  training <- ConTraining[intrain,]
  testing <- ConTraining[-intrain,]
  testingSave = testing
  
  training = training %>% 
  select(-c(ParticipantID, TestTime, ProblemTime, BlankLocation, ProbDuration, SubjectGender, Outcome, Condition)) %>%
  mutate(ProbCorrAdj = factor(.$ProbCorrAdj))
  
  testing = testing %>% 
  select(-c(ParticipantID, TestTime, ProblemTime, BlankLocation, ProbDuration, SubjectGender, Outcome, Condition)) %>%
  mutate(ProbCorrAdj = factor(.$ProbCorrAdj)) 
  
  trctrl <- trainControl(method = "LOOCV")#, number = 10, repeats = 10)
  svmRadial.Con <- train(ProbCorrAdj~., data = training, method = "svmRadial",
                 trControl=trctrl,
                 preProcess = c("center", "scale"),
                 tuneLength = 15)
  AccuracyValList$AccuracyValue[j] = max(svmRadial.Con$results$Accuracy)
  test_pred <- predict(svmRadial.Con, newdata = testing)
  TestData = cbind(testingSave, test_pred)
  TestData.Pred = TestData %>% 
    mutate(PredCorr = case_when(test_pred == ProbCorrAdj ~ 1,
                              test_pred != ProbCorrAdj ~ 0))
  testPredData = confusionMatrix(test_pred, testing$ProbCorrAdj)
  AccuracyValList$TestAccuracy[j] = testPredData$overall[1]
  AccuracyValList$Model[[j]] = svmRadial.Con
  TestData.Pred$MLSet = j

  CorMLTestData_64.Prob = rbind(CorMLTestData_64.Prob,TestData.Pred)
  print(j)
  print(Sys.time())
}
